permutationLabel: Elderly, AKI, undiagnosed myeloma presenting as constipation
summary: 76-year-old man referred with constipation; back and rib pain, weight loss, adjusted calcium 3.21, creatinine 298, Hb 8.9, globulin 58, lytic lesions.

inputs.hpi: Referred with constipation and "possible bowel cancer". Two months of low back and rib pain, worse at night, increasing tiredness, thirst and constipation. Lost 4 kg. Taking ibuprofen for the back pain. No rectal bleeding.

exam.general: Pale, tired. Pulse 90/min, BP 128/74, RR 16, temperature 36.7°C.
exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, faecally loaded; PR: hard stool, no mass.
exam.msk: Tender over the lumbar spine and ribs.
exam.neuro: Lower limb power, sensation and reflexes normal.

imaging.name: XR lumbar spine
imaging.result: Multiple lytic lesions in lumbar vertebral bodies; no vertebral collapse.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Hypercalcaemia with AKI and lytic lesions — suspected multiple myeloma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Hypercalcaemia (3.21), AKI (creatinine 298), anaemia, high globulin and lytic lesions: suspected myeloma. Constipation is secondary.

mustInclude.note: Hypercalcaemia, AKI, anaemia and lytic lesions: missed myeloma is a missed cancer diagnosis.
SfE 2016: IV 0.9% sodium chloride rehydration; a 500 mL AKI fluid challenge does not count.

guideline.name: Society for Endocrinology — Emergency management of acute hypercalcaemia in adult patients
guideline.section: Symptomatic or severe hypercalcaemia: IV 0.9% sodium chloride rehydration guided by fluid status, then IV bisphosphonate; measure PTH to separate PTH-dependent from PTH-independent (malignancy) causes; stop calcium, vitamin D and thiazides
guideline.citation: Walsh J, Gittoes N, Selby P; Society for Endocrinology Clinical Committee. Society for Endocrinology endocrine emergency guidance: emergency management of acute hypercalcaemia in adult patients. Endocr Connect. 2016;5:G9–G11.

guideline.name: NICE NG35 — Myeloma: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Suspected myeloma: serum protein electrophoresis and serum free light chain assay (with urine protein electrophoresis/Bence Jones protein when needed); refer to haematology
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Myeloma: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG35. London: NICE; 2016 (updated 2018).

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: A surgical referral for constipation that is really hypercalcaemia from myeloma. NICE NG35: electrophoresis and light chains; NG148: stop NSAIDs and ACE inhibitors.
